newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Congress delays start of Brazil re-election push.
newsitem.headline: Congress delays start of Brazil re-election push.

text.p: A first meeting of a Brazilian lower house panel to discuss re-election has been put back until 1800 local time/1500 EST on Tuesday, an official said.

The delay was called to give the Brazilian Progressive Party (PPB), one of the biggest parties in Congress, time to name its five committee members. The committee had been due to kick off the re-election debate at 1500 local time/1200 EST, the official said.

The PPB is normally a government ally, but its position on re-election remains unclear as Paulo Maluf, outgoing mayor of Sao Paulo and one of the party's most prominent members, has made public his own presidential ambitions.
The Brazilian Democratic Movement Party (PMDB) named its six members of the committee earlier on Tuesday, ending speculation the party might insist on dealing with re-election only in 1997.
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso hopes to become the first re-elected Brazilian leader since the founding of the Republic in the last century. The next presidential elections are in 1998.

The committee has 40 sessions to discuss and vote on the proposed constitutional amendment to allow presidents, state governors and mayors to run for a second term. If approved by the panel, as expected, the measure goes to the floor of the lower house.
